classification.difficultyReason: The hardest essential parts are (e) and (f). In (e) the student must substitute the tan double-angle formula, clear the fraction and factor out tan x. They then solve tan²x=3 and check that tan x and tan 2x are defined. In (f) they must rewrite tan x as sin x/cos x, cross-multiply and factor out sin x rather than cancelling it. They then solve cos²x=1/2 and note the cos x≠0 restriction. These are routine linked procedures with a few decisions on formula choice, factoring and domain, and no unsignposted insight. The prompt tells the student to use double-angle formulae, and parts (a)-(d) are direct double-angle substitution then factor or quadratic. That is more demanding than the single divide-by-cos tasks in p8-q12. It is less demanding than p30-q12, which needs a harmonic-form representation change, and p17-q9, which needs the exact-value reasoning behind cos x=(1±√5)/4. The statement of part (a) is missing from the supplied prompt (it shows only a full stop). The equation can be recovered from the worked solution as sin2x=√2 sin x. It is the easiest part, so it does not affect the placement.

content.prompt: Use double-angle formulae to solve, for $0\leq x\leq2\pi$:

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}2\sin x\cos x&=\sqrt2\sin x\\2\sin x\cos x-\sqrt2\sin x&=0\\\sin x(2\cos x-\sqrt2)&=0\\\sin x=0\quad&\text{or}\quad\cos x=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\\\therefore x&=0,\frac{\pi}{4},\pi,\frac{7\pi}{4},2\pi\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{aligned}2\sin x\cos x+\sqrt3\cos x&=0\\\cos x(2\sin x+\sqrt3)&=0\\\cos x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\sin x=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\\therefore x&=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{4\pi}{3},\frac{3\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}3\sin x+1-2\sin^2x&=2\\2\sin^2x-3\sin x+1&=0\\(2\sin x-1)(\sin x-1)&=0\\\sin x&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad\sin x=1\\\therefore x&=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}2\cos^2x-1+3\cos x+2&=0\\2\cos^2x+3\cos x+1&=0\\(2\cos x+1)(\cos x+1)&=0\\\cos x&=-\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad\cos x=-1\\\therefore x&=\frac{2\pi}{3},\pi,\frac{4\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2\tan x}{1-\tan^2x}+\tan x&=0\\2\tan x+\tan x(1-\tan^2x)&=0\\\tan x(2+1-\tan^2x)&=0\\\tan x(3-\tan^2x)&=0\\\tan x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\tan x=\pm\sqrt3\\\therefore x&=0,\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{2\pi}{3},\pi,\frac{4\pi}{3},\frac{5\pi}{3},2\pi\end{aligned}$$
All listed values have both $\tan x$ and $\tan2x$ defined.

The original equation requires $\cos x\neq0$.
$$\begin{aligned}2\sin x\cos x&=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\\2\sin x\cos^2x&=\sin x\\\sin x(2\cos^2x-1)&=0\\\sin x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\cos^2x=\frac12\end{aligned}$$
For $\sin x=0$: $x=0,\pi,2\pi$.

For $\cos x=\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $x=\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4},\frac{7\pi}{4}$.

All satisfy $\cos x\neq0$.
